Before we learn how to sing, let’s take a moment and consider the anatomy and physiology of the voice.

Let us follow the voice from the lungs to the lips following the breath stream that starts in the lungs. This breath stream provides a controlled flow of air which powers the vocal folds by setting them into motion.

People who have a ‘low’ breath stream will have sub-optimal vocal production. Yes to breath properly is essential for increasing your volume and the quality of your voice. **

Here is the geeky part; the human larynx has three vital functions.

  • Airway protection (prevention of aspiration)
  • Respiration (breathing)
  • Phonation (talking)

When we speak, the vocal chords vibrate to produce sound and when we breathe the vocal folds open or abduct and allow air-flow from the lungs through the mouth and nose and vice versa.

When we eat, we reflexively stop breathing and the vocal folds approximate to protect the airway and keep food and drink out of the lungs.

The vocal folds do not operate like strings on a violin but actually are more like a vibrating woodwind or reed instrument and are also referred to as the “vibrator or oscillator“.
